name: Konkani

ancestors.notes: Dravidian substrate from pre-IA population of Goa

notes:
Konkani, 22nd scheduled language of India (1992). Spoken in Goa (official), Karnataka, and Kerala. Multiple scripts: Devanagari (official Goa), Kannada, Roman; this spec reads the Devanagari orthography. Strong Dravidian substrate features: retroflex ⟨ळ⟩ = [ɭ]. Close to Marathi but considered a separate language by speakers.

The inherent vowel of a consonant letter is deleted word-finally and in the VC_CV environment, as in the other modern Indo-Aryan languages and unlike Sanskrit, the parent spec; the rules are in allophone_rules.

The mid vowels are /e ɛ o ɔ/ and Devanagari marks no length on ⟨े⟩/⟨ो⟩, so those matras read short, with the open-mid quality as a second candidate. The affricate series /ts dz/ and /tʃ dʒ/ are both written ⟨च⟩/⟨ज⟩ and are not recoverable from the spelling, so both are in the lattice. The rhotic is an alveolar tap and ⟨ह⟩ is a glottal fricative; a sonorant in conjunct with ⟨ह⟩ is one murmured segment (म्हस [mʱəs]).

⟨ऋ⟩/⟨ृ⟩ (vocalic r) were missing from the grapheme table, which silently dropped the segment rather than reading it as the tap-plus-vowel reflex Indo-Aryan languages give the old Sanskrit syllabic r̩ (Masica 1991, ch. 4). The kaikki gold has two occurrences, both after ⟨क⟩: कृपेन [kɾupɛːn] and संस्कृताय [sə̃skɾitɑːj], one with /u/ and one with /i/; /ɾɪ/ is kept as the first candidate and /ɾu/ as the second. ⟨ऑ⟩/⟨ॉ⟩ (candra o) and ⟨ॅ⟩ (candra e) were likewise missing; they mark English-loan vowels Devanagari has no native letter for. The kaikki gold has one occurrence of each — ऑगस्ट [æɡəsʈ], मॅरी [mæɾiː] — both /æ/, so /æ/ is the first candidate for all three graphemes; /ɔ/ and /ɛ/ are kept as second candidates, the values the broader candra-vowel convention documents and Marathi's spec (an adstrate ancestor here) carries.

allophone_rules.notes: Anusvara before a stop is a homorganic nasal CONSONANT, not nasalization of the preceding vowel: रंग [ɾəŋɡ], हिंदी [hindiː], लांब [laːmb], वैकुंठ [ʋəikuɳʈʰ], पांच [paːntʃ]. The anusvara sign writes the nasal of a nasal+stop cluster, and the nasal assimilates to the following stop's place; it is only before a non-stop (fricative, glide, word edge) that it surfaces as nasalization on the vowel -- गांव [ɡãːʋ], हांसप [hãːsəp] (Masica 1991, on the anusvara and homorganic nasals in modern Indo-Aryan Devanagari orthography).

Anusvara before a palatal surfaces as a coronal nasal [n] in this variety rather than assimilating to [ɲ]: gold data shows 7/11 tokens as [n] against 2 as [ɲ]. See KOK_ANUSVARA_VELAR for the general anusvara-as-homorganic-nasal-consonant analysis.
Anusvara -> homorganic retroflex nasal; see KOK_ANUSVARA_VELAR.
Anusvara -> homorganic dental nasal; see KOK_ANUSVARA_VELAR.

Word-final schwa deletion. Konkani does not pronounce the inherent vowel of a word-final consonant letter: गावप is [ɡaːʋəp], not *[ɡaːʋəpə]. The schwa implicit in each consonant of the Devanagari script is obligatorily deleted word-finally in Konkani as in the other modern Indo-Aryan languages, and Sanskrit-style literal readings are not Konkani readings (Masica 1991; Ohala 1983, ch. 5 for the Indo-Aryan rule; Almeida 1989 for Konkani -- edition not consulted). Sanskrit (`sa`, the parent spec) preserves the inherent vowel and declares no such rule, which is why this lives in the Konkani DATA and not in the engine. word_initial=false protects a one-letter monosyllable, whose schwa is the word's only vowel and is never deleted.

Guard for the VC_CV medial rule: the schwa is deleted only when a VOWEL precedes the consonant that carries it. This identity rewrite fires first when the previous lattice slot is a vowel-less consonant (a cluster member carrying a virama) and, because the first matching rule wins, blocks KOK_SCHWA_MEDIAL_*. Same conditioning as Hindi (Ohala 1983, ch. 5; Narasimhan, Sproat & Kiraz 2004).

Medial schwa deletion in the VC_CV environment: a schwa is deleted when a vowel-final segment precedes it and the FOLLOWING consonant carries a vowel of its own -- आयतार [aːjtaːɾ], not *[aːjətaːɾ]. The condition on the following consonant is read off the lattice: a consonant whose inherent vowel was cancelled by a matra surfaces as a BARE consonant phoneme, so followed_by_phoneme = the vowel-less consonant class. The lattice cannot distinguish a matra-bearing consonant from a cluster-initial one, so the rule also fires (over-deletes) before a cluster, e.g. नमस्कार -> nəmskaːɾ where nəməskaːɾ is expected; this limitation is inherited from hi.json's equivalent rule (Ohala 1983, ch. 5; Narasimhan, Sproat & Kiraz 2004; the rule is stated for Konkani in Masica 1991 as the general modern Indo-Aryan schwa syncope).
